trap.segment: Vegans and strict vegetarians: 72% purchase intent but only 1.3 million adults, 2.5% of adults 18-64

items.quote: It enters a protein snack category worth 480 million euros, growing 11% per year, where 27% of French adults bought a protein snack in the last three months [4].
They show the highest purchase intent (72%) but number only 1.3 million adults, 2.5% of the population [5].
Primary target: health-conscious office workers (9.0 million adults, 38% intent) [5].
They buy mainly in supermarkets, which carry 68% of category sales [4]
Secondary target: weekly sport practitioners (17.5 million, 41% intent) [5]
Texture was the most appreciated attribute in Italian blind tests, and 47% preferred Proteo to leading potato crisps, with a further 21% tie [2].
Plant-based products are 18% of the category [4].
The French savoury snack market was 2.9 billion euros in 2024.
The protein snack category was 480 million euros, growing 11% per year from 2021 to 2024.
Channel split of protein snack sales: supermarkets and hypermarkets 68%, specialised sport and organic shops 17%, online 9%, gyms and vending 6% [4].

Verdo Foods S.r.l., Bologna, founded 2020. It makes legume-based savoury snacks. 28 employees, 4.2 M€ turnover in 2024 (almost all in Italy), first profitable year in 2024, second funding round in early 2025 [1]. About 2,300 points of sale in Italy; online shop is 9% of sales [1].
1,500 points of sale in year one is about two-thirds of the 2,300 points of sale built in Italy [1][3].
French consumers know Nutri-Score, which was created in France [3].
Proteo Crisps: oven-baked, chickpea flour and pea protein, 15 g protein per 40 g bag, about 30% more than the leading plant-based protein crisps in Italy.
It is the best-selling line, with 61% of turnover [2].
Plant-based protein snacks are therefore about 86 M€ (own calculation from [4]).
Competitor prices in France [6].

Plant near Bologna at 55% capacity, enough for France without new investment.
If growth continued at 11% per year, it would be roughly 13–15 M€ of retail value by early 2028 (illustrative projection).

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The primary target (health-conscious office workers, 9.0 M at 38% intent) follows from the segment table, with the vegan trap rejected on size (1.3 M, 2.5%) and the mission fit. Channels follow the 68% supermarket share, pricing is explicitly flagged as a direction pending a shelf audit, and the goal-consistency check flags the share versus turnover tension.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: Messages speak to office workers (the 16 h snack, "Craquez malin") and reflect the crisp-first positioning, with channel messages for supermarkets, gyms, organic shops, online and workplace all within the strategy's channel list. The minor gap is that the sport-shop message ("Votre snack d'après-séance") leans on the sport-oriented image the strategy wanted to avoid, and the PR line is generic.
